title: No action against Mineral Resources, Ellison: ASIC
full_text:
That’s a wrap for The Australian’s rolling coverage of business and markets news for Tuesday, September 1.
The conflict in the Middle East is back at the forefront for investors, with renewed fighting in the Strait of Hormuz sending Brent crude futures back above $US90 a barrel and the Dow industrials nearly 400 points lower.
US forces attacked two Iranian rocket launchers in the waterway Sunday, marking the first American strike in weeks and reviving fears that the region could slide back toward all-out conflict. Shortly after the strike, US forces defended against missiles launched at Jordan.
US President Donald Trump says he has ruled out using a nuclear weapon against the Iran, telling a reporter it was a "stupid question" to ask if he was still considering the extreme measure to end the war.
The moves mark the latest bout of volatility for oil prices, which have swung sharply throughout August as hopes for a diplomatic resolution with Iran have waxed and waned. Even so, Brent futures aren’t far from where they were at the start of August.
US stocks retreated, led by the Dow, which dropped 374 points, or 0.7 per cent. The S&P 500 index fell 0.3 per cent and the Nasdaq slipped into the red too,down 0.1 per cent.
US Treasury yields continue to move higher after jumping Friday in response to Fed chairman Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole remarks.
The calendar is relatively light this week in the US as its second-quarter earnings season winds down.
The main event will be Friday’s jobs report, which is expected to show that the US economy added 50,000 jobs in August, compared with a loss of 23,000 the month before.
